page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: What quick lime is
lines: Quick lime is calcium oxide, CaO.
It is made by heating limestone
It is a basic oxide and the cheapest
form of alkali, which is why so many
steps.why: Quick lime is the industrial name for calcium oxide, so the answer opens by naming the compound and where it comes from. It is a basic oxide and cheap, and those two facts are the reason behind every use in the list.
common_mistakes: Confusing quick lime with slaked lime. Quick lime is CaO; slaked lime is Ca(OH)₂.
Writing CaCO₃ as quick lime. Calcium carbonate is limestone, the raw material it is made from.
steps.memory_tip: Limestone heated gives quick lime, CaO, and carbon dioxide.
steps.margin_note: Name CaO and keep it apart from slaked lime before listing the uses.

steps.label: Its uses
lines: 5. as a basic flux in metallurgy, where
it removes silica as calcium silicate:
steps.why: Cement is written first because it is the use met most often; the alkali, sugar and dye industries follow. The last use shows quick lime acting as a base — it takes up the acidic oxide silica and carries it away as slag. In the alkali industry lime is slaked first, and the slaked lime converts sodium carbonate into caustic soda.
common_mistakes: Writing only that it is used in buildings. Name the industries: cement, alkali, sugar and dye stuffs.
Giving the uses of slaked lime, such as whitewashing. This question is about quick lime, CaO.
steps.memory_tip: Cement first, then the alkali, sugar and dye industries.
steps.margin_note: A numbered list of four or five named uses is a comfortable length.

insider_note: Quick lime and slaked lime are asked about separately, so name CaO at the start and keep the whitewashing use out of this answer.
